# Réponse proposée (à coller sur GitHub seulement si tu es d'accord)

Thanks, that matches what we found. Most of the 294 "first lane of a phi" programs are if/else joins. One edge brings a real descriptor (an `s_load_dwordx4` from a table), and the other edges bring VGPRs that can't be a descriptor (computed values, a buffer load, an input VGPR). Lanes on those edges never reach the access.

The `up/firstlane-phi` branch now handles this in two steps:

1. **Junk edges.** On a join, a path whose dwords can't be a descriptor becomes "no descriptor" (heap index 0). This only applies when at least one other path is a real descriptor. LDS reads are not treated as junk.
2. **`v_readfirstlane` outside a waterfall loop.** If the read isn't compared with every lane's own dwords in the same loop, it's not a waterfall. The console then uses the first active lane's descriptor for every lane, so we do the same: the handle index is `WaveReadLaneFirst` of the per-lane heap index, taken where the console reads the dwords, and the handle stays uniform. A loop that compares only some of the dwords still fails on purpose, because heap indexes can't reproduce the hardware result there.

Tests cover both cases, and each new test fails without its change. I'll post the corpus numbers after the next offline translate run.
